references.text: Moses gave the command to hang the condemned on a tree and take down the body before sunset, which Joshua follows exactly in this text.
The law required that a hanged person be taken down before evening, and Joshua obeys this by taking down the five kings at sunset.
Joshua treated the king of Ai in the same way—hung on a tree until evening, then taken down and thrown at the city gate with stones piled over him.
Earlier in the same chapter, the five kings were found hidden in the cave at Makkedah, and large stones were rolled in front of the entrance.
Absalom was cast into a large pit in the forest and covered with a great heap of stones, similar treatment to that given to the five kings.
Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian, were killed by Gideon, showing a similar pattern of executing enemy kings.
David killed Goliath and took his head as a sign of victory, similar to how Joshua dealt with the defeated kings.
